# AirBridge

> Open-source AirDrop alternative for Android, Mac and Windows. It shares the clipboard, sends files, lets one keyboard and mouse control several devices, shows a phone's calls and notifications on the computer, and mirrors the phone's screen. Everything runs on the local network: no account, no cloud, no server.

AirBridge is three native apps (Android in Kotlin, macOS in Swift, Windows in C#) that speak one documented protocol. Licensed under the GNU AGPL v3. Android 8.0 or newer; macOS 26.1 or newer for the current source; Windows 10 (2004) or 11. Linux and iOS are not started. Released builds (August 2026, v2.1) are on the Releases page; the source in the repository is newer.

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/ShazanZaidii/AirBridge/blob/main/README.md): what it does, install, privacy, questions people ask
- [Protocol](https://github.com/ShazanZaidii/AirBridge/blob/main/docs/protocol.md): the wire protocol all apps follow (discovery, pairing, encryption, clipboard, files, remote control, calls, battery)
- [AirWeb](https://github.com/ShazanZaidii/AirBridge/blob/main/docs/airweb.md): sharing files with devices that only have a browser
